title: Vimta Labs Ltd-$ - 524394 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vimta Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.6% YoY to INR1,120 million, with EBITDA margin of 37.6% and a net debt-free balance sheet.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 million, up 16.6% YoY, with EBITDA of INR421 million (37.6% margin) and PAT of INR211 million (18.9% margin). For FY26, total income reached INR4,163 million (up 19.5%), EBITDA INR1,489 million (35.8% margin) and PAT INR775 million (up 16.1%). Management said Q4 was helped by pre-clinical and seasonal food testing, but some expected growth did not materialise, and the company missed its earlier INR500 million annualised run-rate goal. The company entered biologics contract research (biologics and peptides) in FY26, with FY27 framed as a year of execution with no meaningful revenue expected yet.

financial_highlights.change: +16.6% YoY (vs INR961 million); +11.5% QoQ as stated
+15.2% YoY as stated (compared with INR183 million)

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR650 million; net debt-free

segments.name: Pharma research and testing
segments.commentary: Largest contributor in FY26 with good domestic and international demand; management says pharma and food together make up about 90% of revenue. Pharma analytical work is mostly for ANDA, 505(b)(2) and NDA product release and filings, and FTE-based work is limited to analytical services.

segments.name: Food testing
segments.commentary: Good momentum in FY26 and a strong Q4 seasonally; last fortnight of March was hit by the war, given exposure to exporters and import testing at NFL Navi Mumbai.

segments.name: Electronics and electrical testing
segments.commentary: Management called FY26 not very exciting after leadership challenges on technical, operational and BD sides, now said to be fixed; most customers retained, with a hope for stronger movement.

segments.name: Environmental testing
segments.commentary: Very small part of the business; company has exited EIA and now does only post-project monitoring, with revenue held flat and no strong growth focus.

segments.name: Biologics / peptides contract R&D
segments.commentary: Newly launched in FY26; infrastructure, systems and people are in place, with inquiries from Europe, India and the US. Management expects FY27 to be a year of traction, with margins likely similar to the core business, a few percentage points either way.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins to be corrected by about 1-2% from current levels due to input costs and manpower, but broadly maintained, with revenue growth offsetting this.
Management called 20-25% CAGR over the next three to four years a stretch but doable, and said that is the annual target.
Management intends to keep Q4-type momentum (about INR120-130 crore quarterly revenue, per the analyst's framing) but did not commit to a number.
Biologics CRO is expected to start in FY27; the aim is to onboard a few good clients and deliver well, with revenue significance not expected in the first year.
Utilisation of the new facility will rise gradually, a little more in FY27 and more in FY28.
US subsidiary approved to be closer to customers; no investment amount disclosed.
capex_capacity: New expansion facility is operational; management said it should cover growth for four to five years, with utilisation to build over FY27 and FY28.
Biologics and peptides CRO infrastructure, equipment, systems and people are said to be ready.
No firm plans for capital deployment, acquisitions, new capacity or fundraising; management said no rights issue or equity raise is needed now.
US subsidiary approved; investment amount not disclosed and it is framed as a customer-proximity move with little tariff benefit.
demand_pricing: Management sees good visibility for pharma, food and electronics testing, driven by outsourcing growth of about 7-12% in the industries served.
Pharma pipelines are shifting toward large molecules, and smaller companies are growing in R&D; the company sees more outsourcing opportunities as a result.
Price competition is strong in routine, low-tech services, while specialty, science-intensive services give the company an edge; food is more commoditised.
War impact: input materials and consumables costs are up slightly, and supply-chain lead times are longer; the full future impact is uncertain.
Pharma was hit by US tariffs last year, which management says have since been reversed.
Indian pharma analytical testing market is expected to reach about USD300 million by 2030, versus a USD9.7 billion global figure cited in the company's slides.

qa_highlights.question: Margin profile by vertical and biologics timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are not split by service line; the company treats it as one service. Biologics is ready in terms of infrastructure, but too early to say when it will be significant.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook and whether 20-25% CAGR is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 20-25% CAGR a stretch but doable and the annual target. Visibility is good in pharma, food and electronics.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Indian testing market small relative to global?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said R&D is much smaller in India than in developed markets, and that low-value testing rarely justifies shipping samples overseas.

qa_highlights.question: Margins in the biologics business?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to be around the core level, a few percentage points either way; early projects are domestic and input costs are high, with better margins expected once overseas clients come on board.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for the INR500 crore annualised revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: The target was originally to reach it by FY25; the company aims for Q4 run-rates in FY26 but missed due to external headwinds. Management remains hopeful but cautious.

qa_highlights.question: Capital deployment and fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm plans for cash deployment, acquisitions or capacity expansion, and no fundraising is needed at present.

risks_watch: Geopolitical conflict affecting input costs, consumables and supply-chain lead times, with the last fortnight of March already affected in food testing.
EBITDA margin correction of 1-2% expected from input costs and manpower; FY26 margin of 35.8% may not hold.
Biologics ramp-up is at an early stage; margins are expected to be lower initially and client wins are not yet confirmed.
Electronics and electrical testing is recovering from leadership gaps and its performance is still unproven.
Revenue is uneven by quarter (food is seasonal), and the company missed its INR500 million annualised run-rate goal.
Limited disclosure on segment margins and FTE/FFS mix makes external tracking difficult.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term opportunity and demand, but cautious on the near term, with repeated references to geopolitical uncertainty, cost pressure and external headwinds. Management was candid that Q4 fell short of its internal expectations and was reluctant to give hard numbers on margins, biologics revenue and capital deployment.
key_quotes: Vimta continues to maintain very healthy EBITDA margins, clocking about 35.8% in FY '26, which we believe are among the best in the industry even by global standards.
It's a stretch number, but definitely doable. And that's what we target each year.
Our goal was to hit INR500 crores by last year, but because of divestment of diagnostics, we said we will try and get to those run rates by Q4.

adds.what: New expansion facility (already operational; said to cover growth for 4-5 years, utilisation to build over FY27-FY28)
Biologics and peptides CRO infrastructure, equipment, systems and people (ready; revenue significance not expected in FY27 first year)

growth.why: Management targets a 20-25% revenue CAGR over 3-4 years (called a stretch but doable, midpoint 22.5%), backed mainly by pharma/food demand and outsourcing trends, the operational new facility and a biologics CRO launched in FY26 with no meaningful FY27 revenue expected; no firm orders or contract numbers were given, and the company missed its INR500 million run-rate goal.

mgmt.note: Electronics and electrical testing leadership challenges on technical, operational and BD sides were discussed as fixed; no specific change or date given in the brief.
